summary: Kim Knott is an indology and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Leeds (circa 1983-2012) and Lancaster University (circa 2012).

Kim Plofker works in indology and history/archaeology. She earned her bachelor's from Haverford College and her PhD from Brown University under David Pingree. She held positions at MIT, Brown, Utrecht, and Union College, becoming Associate Professor in 2019.

Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University. She was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and served as professor at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University.

Kimiaki Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. His career includes posts at the University of Tokyo, Beijing Center for Japanese Studies, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a computational linguistics scholar educated at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He was Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki from circa 1989 to 2013 and directed its BAULT research community.
Kin Cheung is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo.
King Chung Lo is an indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar of indology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under Jacqueline Suthren Hirst.

Kirby Flower Smith was an indology scholar who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (circa 1889-1918) and directed the American Academy in Rome (1914-1915).
Kirill Solonin works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) and Renmin University of China (circa 2013).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an indology scholar who was educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and indology. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya and Gopinath Bhattacharya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, he taught at the Fourth Higher School before serving as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University from 1910 to 1928.

Kiyoaki Okuda is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf. He held posts as professor at Shitennoji University and director of the Shitennoji Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Kiyoshi Kato was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at Otani University under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji Kobe Betsuin and Hyanghwa Girls' Vocational School.
Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida from circa 1917 to 1920. He subsequently held posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (circa 1924-1927).

Kiyoshi Okano is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University, serving as associate professor and later professor of Indian philosophy.

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Rissho University. He held posts at Rissho University as a lecturer and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra.

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kyoto University (circa 1935-1969) and Ryukoku University (circa 1969-1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Shitennoji University, Tsurumi Women's University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
